title: Video in 100 KB
lede: A 5-second underwater clip (720p, 10 frames per second) squeezed into 100 KB, small enough for a satellite or cellular link, and encoded on the camera's own Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W. Drag the divider: left is the original video frame, right is the same frame after the 100 KB encode. Click a view for full screen and zoom to 1:1.

facts.label: 720p, 10 fps, as sent (12× smaller than the camera's own 2 Mbit/s recording)
calm pool scenes (90 ≈ looks like the original)
worst clip: a diver crossing the card (70 = good)
encode time and memory on a Pi Zero 2 W (emulated, calibrated)

notes: AV1 (open, royalty-free) at full 720p beats every lower resolution or frame rate we tried at the same 100 KB.
Today's H.264 at the same size is visibly softer and blockier where things move (VMAF 67 on the hardest clip).
Limit: a busy scene (diver close, bubbles) drops to about VMAF 59, below 'watchable'. Sending a background image once a day lifts it to 64.
Pi time and memory were measured in a Pi-matched container and scaled to real Pi Zero 2 W runs; a check on the real camera comes next.
footer: Six 5-second clips from the 2026-10-14 pool test (two cameras, three rounds, colour card at 2 m). Quality score: VMAF (0–100, Netflix's perceptual video metric), every frame against the original. Method and full numbers: rig repo compression_study/video_100k/RESULTS.md.
